stem: Imagine that you are an explorer who has discovered an isolated land mass in the middle of the Pacific Ocean. You find a predator that resembles a North American wolf except that it lays eggs. You name it the "mid-ocean wolf." The physical similarity between the mid-ocean wolf and the North American wolf is most likely due to which of the following factors?

options.A: inheritance of the characteristics from a recent common ancestor
options.B: natural selection that favors the evolution of homologous structures
options.C: natural selection that favors similar traits for organisms with similar ecological roles
options.D: similarities in prey species

why: An egg-laying 'wolf' can't be a close relative of real wolves (mammals that give birth), so the resemblance isn't inherited. Similar lifestyles (both are predators) favor similar body shapes. That's convergent evolution, which produces analogous traits, not homologous ones.

stem: Which of the following observations helped Darwin shape his concept of descent with modification?

options.A: Fewer species live on islands than on the nearest continents.
options.B: Birds live on islands located farther from the mainland than the birds' maximum nonstop flight distance.
options.C: Species diversity declines farther from the equator.
options.D: South American temperate plants are more similar to the tropical plants of South America than to the temperate plants of Europe.

why: Darwin noticed that species are more like their geographic neighbors than like species in a similar climate far away. That fits descent from local ancestors, not separate creation for each climate. The other choices are real patterns, but they aren't what shaped his thinking.

stem: DNA sequences in many human genes are very similar to the sequences of corresponding genes in chimpanzees. The most likely explanation for this result is that ________.

options.A: chimpanzees evolved from humans
options.B: convergent evolution led to the DNA similarities
options.C: humans and chimpanzees share a relatively recent common ancestor
options.D: humans evolved from chimpanzees

why: Very similar DNA means little time has passed since the two lineages split from a shared ancestor. Neither species evolved from the other: both are modern, living branches. Convergence happens to traits under similar pressures, not to most of the genome.

stem: The upper forelimbs of humans and bats have fairly similar skeletal structures, whereas the corresponding bones in whales have very different shapes and proportions. However, genetic data suggest that all three kinds of organisms diverged from a common ancestor at about the same time. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for these data?

options.A: Natural selection in an aquatic environment resulted in significant changes to whale forelimb anatomy.
options.B: Whales are not properly classified as mammals.
options.C: Genes mutate faster in whales than in humans or bats.
options.D: Forelimb evolution was adaptive in people and bats, but not in whales.

why: All three lineages split at about the same time, so the whale's very different forelimb must come from strong selection in water (flippers for swimming), not from more time. The bones are still homologous; they've just been reshaped.

stem: Which of the following is not an observation or inference on which natural selection is based?

options.A: Only a fraction of an individual's offspring may survive.
options.B: There is heritable variation among individuals.
options.C: Poorly adapted individuals never produce offspring.
options.D: Species produce more offspring than the environment can support.

why: Natural selection says poorly adapted individuals tend to leave FEWER offspring, not zero. 'Never' is too absolute. The other three are Darwin's actual observations and inferences: overproduction, heritable variation, and that only some offspring survive.

stem: Within six months of effectively using methicillin to treat S. aureus infections in a community, all new S. aureus infections were caused by MRSA. How can this best be explained?

options.A: Some drug-resistant bacteria were present at the start of treatment, and natural selection increased their frequency.
options.B: In response to the drug, S. aureus began making drug-resistant versions of the protein targeted by the drug.
options.C: S. aureus evolved to resist vaccines.
options.D: A patient must have become infected with MRSA from another community.

why: The drug didn't cause the resistance. A few resistant bacteria already existed, the drug killed the susceptible ones, and the survivors reproduced. Choice B is the classic wrong idea that organisms change because they need to.

stem: Fossil evidence indicates that modern whales and other cetaceans (dolphins and porpoises) are closely related to even-toed ungulates (hippopotamuses, pigs, deer, and cows). Which of the following predictions would you make if you wanted to test this idea using the amino acid sequence of hemoglobin?

options.A: Hemoglobin sequences of whales will be more similar to hippopotamuses than to a fossil common ancestor of all even-toed ungulates (assume we can discover the amino acid sequence from a fossil).
options.B: Hemoglobin sequences of whales will be more similar to dogs than to hippopotamuses.
options.C: Hemoglobin sequences of whales will be more similar to hippopotamuses than to horses.
options.D: Hemoglobin sequences of whales will be more similar to gorillas than to hippopotamuses.

why: Use the diagram: whales and hippos share a more recent common ancestor than whales and horses do, so their hemoglobin should be more similar. Making that kind of prediction is how molecular data tests a fossil-based hypothesis. (Open the PDF to see the tree.)

stem: Which of the following statements is accurate if we view evolution both as a pattern and a process?

options.A: To study evolution as a pattern we draw on information from many other scientific fields, while to study evolution as a process we study factors that cause changes in populations.
options.B: To study evolution as a pattern we study data from current day populations, while to study evolution as a process we rely on data from the past.
options.C: To study evolution as a pattern we rely on data from the past, while to study evolution as a process we study data from current day populations.
options.D: To study evolution as a pattern we study factors that cause changes in populations, while to study evolution as a process we draw on information from many other scientific fields.

why: The PATTERN of evolution (what changed) comes from many fields: fossils, anatomy, biogeography and molecules. The PROCESS (how it changes) is studied through the mechanisms that change populations: selection, drift and gene flow.

stem: Darwin used the phrase "descent with modification" to explain which of the following ideas?

options.A: the unity of life
options.B: the diversity of life
options.C: both the unity and diversity of life
options.D: descent of all organisms from a single, ancient ancestor

why: 'Descent' explains UNITY: shared ancestry gives organisms shared features. 'Modification' explains DIVERSITY: lineages adapted to different environments. The phrase covers both at once.

stem: Which of the following statements is most consistent with data obtained from the fossil record?

options.A: Geologic changes occur quickly on Earth.
options.B: Older strata carry fossils that differ greatly from living organisms.
options.C: Unused body parts decrease in size.
options.D: Organisms have an innate drive to increase in complexity.

why: Deeper (older) rock layers hold fossils that look less like living species, which is what gradual change over long times predicts. Choices C and D are Lamarck-style ideas that the fossil record doesn't support.

stem: The figure shows an outcrop of sedimentary rock whose strata are labeled A-D. If x indicates the earliest appearance of fossils of two closely related species, neither of which is extinct, then their remains may be found in which of these strata?

options.A: strata A and B only
options.B: stratum A only
options.C: strata A, B, and C only
options.D: all four strata

why: Fossils can only show up in layers laid down AFTER a species first appeared, so strata at or above the x marks. Living species keep appearing in the youngest layers. Strata in a cross-section are read from the bottom (oldest) up. (Open the PDF to see the strata figure.)

stem: James Hutton and Charles Lyell provided which of the following ideas that paved the way for Darwin's thinking?

options.A: the surface features of Earth were formed by catastrophic events and those events are still occurring
options.B: the surface features of Earth were formed slowly and gradually and the geological processes are still at work
options.C: the surface features of Earth were formed by catastrophic events and the fossil record showed that species have evolved
options.D: the surface features of Earth were formed gradually and the fossil record showed that species have evolved

why: Hutton and Lyell argued that slow, gradual processes still acting today (erosion, sedimentation) shaped the Earth, which implies a very old Earth. Darwin applied the same 'slow and gradual' thinking to living things. Catastrophism was Cuvier's idea.

stem: Which of the following factors contribute to limiting the capacity of organisms to overreproduce?

options.A: inability of individuals to tolerate the physical conditions, lack of food, and mortality from predators
options.B: lack of food, mortality from predators, and production of many offspring per pair of parents
options.C: inability of individuals to tolerate the physical conditions, production of many offspring per pair of parents, and abundance of food
options.D: abundance of food, mortality from predators, and inability of individuals to tolerate the physical conditions

why: Overreproduction is held in check by limits: harsh conditions, limited food, and predators. Choices with 'abundant food' or 'many offspring per pair' are things that INCREASE population growth, not limit it.

stem: Of the following anatomical structures, which is most homologous to the bones in the wings of a bird?

options.A: bony rays in the tail fin of a flying fish
options.B: bones in the flippers of a whale
options.C: chitinous struts in the wings of a butterfly
options.D: bones in the hind limbs of a kangaroo

why: Homologous means the same underlying structure inherited from a common ancestor. Bird wings and whale flippers are both modified tetrapod FORELIMBS. Kangaroo hind limbs are the wrong limb, and fish fin rays and insect wings are analogous at best.

stem: Which of the following statements about vestigial structures is accurate?

options.A: A vestigial structure in species A can be analogous to a functional structure in Species B.
options.B: A vestigial structure in species A did not have a function in past ancestors.
options.C: A vestigial structure in species A can be homologous to a functional structure in species B.
options.D: A vestigial structure in species A is likely an example of convergent evolution with a structure in species B.

why: A vestigial structure, like the whale's pelvic bones, is a leftover of a structure that worked in an ancestor. It's homologous to working versions in related species, like the pelvis and legs of other mammals. Choice B is wrong because it DID have a function in the ancestors.

stem: Which of the following statements best describes Linnaeus' method of classifying organisms?

options.A: Linnaeus grouped organisms into increasingly more inclusive categories.
options.B: Linnaeus grouped organisms according to the linear hierarchy of the scala naturae.
options.C: Linnaeus grouped organisms into increasingly more complex categories.
options.D: Linnaeus grouped organisms according to their geographical location.

why: Linnaeus built nested groups: species inside genera, genera inside families, and so on up to kingdom. Each level is more inclusive. He grouped by similarity, not by 'complexity' or by location.

stem: Continental drift (plate tectonics) has moved continents around the globe. Which of the following predictions would be most likely?

options.A: No species will occur on all continents.
options.B: The most recently separated continents will have the most closely related species.
options.C: There is not enough information to make a prediction.
options.D: Most species will occur only on one continent.

why: Continents that split recently have had less time for their species to diverge, so their species should be the most closely related. That's biogeography used as evidence for evolution.

stem: A species of mouse that is preyed on by owls (which can see color) at dawn and dusk varies in coat color between dark and light brown. Under which of the following conditions will NO evolution occur if climate change results in the soil color becoming darker?

options.A: Dark-colored mice are more likely to be eaten by owls.
options.B: There is no variability in the genes that control coat color.
options.C: Light-colored mice produce more offspring than dark-colored mice.
options.D: There is no way to make a prediction.

why: Evolution by natural selection needs HERITABLE VARIATION. If every mouse has the same coat-color genes, there's nothing to select, so the population can't evolve no matter how the soil changes.

stem: Which of the following statements about evolutionary trees is accurate?

options.A: Evolutionary trees are considered evolutionary theories.
options.B: Evolutionary trees are developed when they are confirmed by fossil evidence.
options.C: Evolutionary trees are considered evolutionary hypotheses.
options.D: Evolutionary trees cannot be tested by gathering more evidence.

why: Trees are HYPOTHESES about relationships. They can be tested and revised as new fossil or DNA evidence comes in, which rules out choices B and D.

stem: Over long periods of time, many cave-dwelling organisms have lost their eyes. Tapeworms have lost their digestive systems. Whales have lost their hind limbs. How can natural selection account for these losses?

options.A: Under particular circumstances that persisted for long periods, natural selection reduced each of these structures because they presented greater costs than benefits.
options.B: The ancestors of these organisms experienced harmful mutations that forced them to lose these structures.
options.C: Natural selection accounts for these losses by the principle of use and disuse.
options.D: Natural selection cannot account for losses, but can only account for new structures and functions.

why: Structures cost energy and can be a liability (eyes are vulnerable in caves, for example). When a structure costs more than it helps, individuals with reduced versions leave more offspring. Use and disuse (choice C) is Lamarck's idea, not natural selection.

stem: Cystic fibrosis is a genetic disorder in humans where the person has two homozygous recessive alleles for the gene. If the disease is left untreated, it causes severe health problems in the individual. If 9 in 10,000 newborn babies have the disease, what are the expected frequencies of the dominant (A1 ) and recessive (A2 ) alleles according to the Hardy-Weinberg equation?
why: Hardy–Weinberg: affected (aa) = q² = 9/10,000 = 0.0009. Then q = √0.0009 = 0.03 and p = 1 − 0.03 = 0.97. Choice C is the trap: 0.0392 is 2pq for q = 0.02, not an allele frequency.

stem: Natural selection changes allele frequencies because some ________ survive and reproduce better than others.

options.A: loci
options.B: individuals
options.C: species
options.D: alleles

why: Selection acts on INDIVIDUALS: each one survives and reproduces or doesn't. But only POPULATIONS evolve, through changes in allele frequencies across generations.

stem: One population of a species has 25 individuals, all with genotype AA; a second population of this species has 40 individuals, all with genotype aa. Assume that these populations live far apart but in similar environmental conditions. Based on this information, the observed genetic variation most likely resulted from ________.

options.A: gene flow
options.B: directional selection
options.C: genetic drift
options.D: nonrandom mating

why: Two small, isolated populations in SIMILAR environments ended up fixed for different alleles. Since selection pressures are the same, chance is the best explanation, and that's genetic drift. Gene flow would make them MORE alike.

stem: No two people are genetically identical, except for identical twins. The main source of genetic variation among humans is ________.

options.A: environmental effects
options.B: the reshuffling of alleles in sexual reproduction
options.C: genetic drift
options.D: new mutations that occurred in the preceding generation

why: New mutations each generation are rare. Most of the differences between siblings and strangers come from shuffling existing alleles: crossing over, independent assortment, and random fertilization.

stem: If the nucleotide variability of a locus equals 0%, what is the gene variability and number of alleles at that locus?

options.A: gene variability > 0%; number of alleles = 2
options.B: gene variability = 0%; number of alleles = 1
options.C: gene variability = 0%; number of alleles = 0
options.D: gene variability = 0%; number of alleles = 2

why: If no nucleotides vary at a locus, every copy of the gene is identical. That means there's exactly ONE allele and gene variability is 0%. 'Zero alleles' would mean the gene doesn't exist.

stem: A fruit fly population has a gene with two alleles, A1 and A2. Tests show that 70% of the gametes produced in the population contain the A1 allele. If the population is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, what proportion of the flies carry both A1 and A2?
why: 70% of gametes carry A1, so p = 0.7 and q = 0.3. Flies carrying BOTH alleles are heterozygotes: 2pq = 2(0.7)(0.3) = 0.42. 0.49 is p² (A1A1) and 0.21 forgets the 2.

stem: The value of the Hardy-Weinberg equation is that it allows scientists to perform which of the following assessments?

options.A: to provide proof that natural selection is acting
options.B: to measure the effects of gene flow among populations
options.C: to detect whether an evolutionary force is acting on a population
options.D: to predict the percentage of people in a population that is homozygous for the recessive allele that causes a genetic disease

why: Hardy–Weinberg describes a population that is NOT evolving. If real data don't match its predictions, some evolutionary force (selection, drift, gene flow, mutation or nonrandom mating) is at work. It tells you THAT something is acting, not which force or that it's selection.

stem: In a Hardy-Weinberg population with two alleles A1 and A2 that are in equilibrium, the frequency of allele A2 is 0.1. What is the frequency of individuals with A1 A1 genotype?

Two scientists measured the snout-to-vent (anus) length of Galápagos marine iguanas (lizards) and observed the percent survival of different-sized animals, all of the same age. The graph shows the log snout-vent length (SVL, a measure of overall body size) plotted against the percent survival of these different size classes for males and females. (Data from M. Wikelski and L. Michael Romero. Body size, performance and fitness in Galapagos marine iguanas. Integrative and Comparative Biology 43:376-386 [2003].) Currently, the only predators of Galápagos marine iguanas are Galápagos hawks. Although small iguanas can sprint faster than large iguanas, iguana body size is not correlated with risk of hawk predation. If predators (for example, cats) that preferentially catch and eat slower iguanas are introduced to the island, iguana body size is likely to ________ in the absence of other factors; the iguanas would then be under ________ selection.

options.A: decrease; directional
options.B: increase; directional
options.C: decrease; disruptive
options.D: increase; disruptive

why: New predators that catch SLOWER iguanas favor faster ones, and smaller iguanas sprint faster. Selection pushes body size toward one extreme (smaller), which is DIRECTIONAL selection toward a decrease.

stem: Imagine a human population with an extremely low frequency of sickle cell alleles. Which of the following changes is most likely in the human population 15 generations after introducing a mosquito population that carries the malaria parasite?

options.A: a decrease in the number of mosquito bites
options.B: an increase in red blood cells without nuclei
options.C: an increase in the mutation rate of the hemoglobin gene
options.D: an increase in the sickle cell allele

why: Malaria makes heterozygotes (sickle-cell carriers) survive better: heterozygote advantage. Over generations the sickle-cell allele's frequency rises. The mosquitoes don't change human mutation rates.

stem: A biologist doing a long-term study on a wild spider population observes increased variation in silk thickness. Which of the following processes is the most likely to be affecting the spider population?

options.A: directional selection
options.B: disruptive selection
options.C: stabilizing selection
options.D: genetic drift

why: More VARIATION means both extremes (thin and thick silk) are being favored over the middle. That's disruptive selection. Stabilizing selection would REDUCE variation, and directional selection shifts the average.

stem: In which of the following situations would genetic drift most likely cause evolution?

options.A: The population has inherited traits better suited to a different environment.
options.B: A sudden change in the environment drastically increases the population size.
options.C: Chance events cause allele frequencies to fluctuate unpredictably.
options.D: The size of the gene pool increases because a smaller group establishes a new population.

why: Genetic drift is chance changes in allele frequencies, strongest in small populations. Choice C is basically its definition. A population getting LARGER weakens drift.

stem: Most Swiss starlings (birds) produce four to five eggs in each clutch. Starlings producing more or less eggs have reduced fitness. Which of the following terms best describes this situation?

options.A: stabilizing selection
options.B: disruptive selection
options.C: sexual selection
options.D: directional selection

why: The middle value (4–5 eggs) has the highest fitness and both extremes do worse. Favoring the average is STABILIZING selection.

stem: A proficient engineer can easily design skeletal structures that are more functional than those currently found in the forelimbs of such diverse mammals as horses, whales, and bats. Which of the following statements best explains why the actual forelimbs of these mammals do not seem to be optimally arranged?

options.A: Natural selection is generally limited to modifying structures that were present in previous generations and in previous species.
options.B: Natural selection has not had sufficient time to create the optimal design in each case, but will do so given enough time.
options.C: Although we may not consider the fit between the current skeletal arrangements and their functions excellent, we should not doubt that natural selection ultimately produces the best design.
options.D: In many cases, phenotype is determined by genotype and the environment.

why: Selection can only modify what's already there; it can't start over from scratch. Every mammal forelimb is a reworked version of the same ancestral bones, so the designs are compromises. Choice B wrongly treats evolution as moving toward a perfect goal.

stem: In those parts of equatorial Africa where the malaria parasite is most common, the sickle-cell allele constitutes 20% of the hemoglobin alleles in the human gene pool. In the United States, the parasite that causes malaria is not present, but the sickle cell allele is present in many African-Americans whose ancestors were from equatorial Africa. Which of the following processes are most likely acting on the sickle-cell allele in the United States, and in equatorial Africa?

options.A: stabilizing selection in the United States; disruptive selection in equatorial Africa
options.B: directional selection in the United States; stabilizing selection in equatorial Africa
options.C: disruptive selection in the United States; stabilizing selection in equatorial Africa
options.D: directional selection in the United States; disruptive selection in equatorial Africa

why: U.S.: no malaria, so the allele only causes harm and selection steadily lowers it. That's directional. Africa: heterozygotes do best, which keeps both alleles at an intermediate balance. The key calls that stabilizing (it's balancing selection through heterozygote advantage).

stem: Suppose 64% of the individuals in a remote mountain village can taste phenylthiocarbamide (PTC) and must, therefore, have at least one copy of the dominant PTC taster allele. If this population conforms to Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium for this gene, what percent of the population must be heterozygous for this trait?
why: 64% can taste, so 36% can't. Non-tasters are homozygous recessive: q² = 0.36, q = 0.6 and p = 0.4. Heterozygotes: 2pq = 2(0.4)(0.6) = 0.48 = 48%. Common mistake: starting from 0.64 as if it were p².

stem: Researchers studying a small milkweed population note that some plants produce a toxin and other plants do not. They identify the gene responsible for toxin production. One allele (T1 ) codes for an enzyme that makes the toxin, and another allele (T2 ) codes for a nonfunctional enzyme that cannot produce the toxin. Heterozygotes produce an intermediate amount of toxin. The researchers measured the abundance of each of the three possible genotypes and compared those numbers to the expected numbers if the population were in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. Those numbers are shown in the chart. Hardy-Weinberg expected numbers Observed numbers T 1 T1 98 112 T 1 T2 84 56 T 2 T2 18 32 Based on these data, which answer correctly identifies whether the population is likely in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium?

options.A: No, there are more heterozygotes than expected.
options.B: Yes, the population appears to be in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.
options.C: No, there are more homozygotes than expected.
options.D: More information is needed to answer this question.

why: Compare observed with expected: T1T1 is 112 vs 98 (more), T2T2 is 32 vs 18 (more), T1T2 is 56 vs 84 (fewer). There are more homozygotes and fewer heterozygotes than Hardy–Weinberg predicts, so the population is NOT in equilibrium.

stem: In a Hardy-Weinberg population with two alleles A1 and A2 that are in equilibrium, the frequency of the allele A2 is 0.3. What is the frequency of individuals that are homozygous for this allele?
why: Homozygous for A2 means q². With q = 0.3, q² = 0.3 × 0.3 = 0.09. Choice B (9.0) is the classic decimal mistake.

stem: Restriction enzymes in bacteria protect the bacteria from successful attack by bacteriophages, whose genomes can be degraded by the restriction enzymes. The bacterial genomes are not vulnerable to these restriction enzymes because bacterial DNA is methylated. This situation selects for bacteriophages whose genomes are also methylated. As new strains of resistant bacteriophages become more prevalent, they in turn select for bacteria whose genomes are not methylated and whose restriction enzymes instead degrade methylated DNA. Which of the following factors is most likely to cause the changes?

options.A: evolutionary imbalance
options.B: heterozygote advantage
options.C: neutral variation
options.D: frequency-dependent selection

why: Methylated phages do best when methylated phages are RARE, because bacteria haven't evolved defenses against them yet. As they become common, bacteria adapt and their advantage shrinks. When fitness depends on how common a type is, that's frequency-dependent selection.

stem: A species of moth lays eggs on oak trees in spring and summer. Spring caterpillars eat oak flowers and look like oak flowers. Summer caterpillars eat oak leaves and look like twigs. To investigate how the same population of moths can produce such variable caterpillars, a researcher collected eggs from a population of moths and allowed them to hatch and grow under the conditions shown in the table below. Treatment 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 Temperature Spring-like Spring-like Spring-like Spring-like Summer-like Summer-like Summer-like Summer-like Day Length Spring-like Spring-like Summer-like Summer-like Spring-like Spring-like Summer-like Summer-like Food Oak flowers Oak leaves Oak flowers Oak leaves Oak flowers Oak leaves Oak flowers Oak leaves Comparison of which treatments would allow the researcher to assess the effect of food type on caterpillar morphology?

options.A: 1, 2, 4, and 5 versus 3, 6, 7, and 8
options.B: 1, 2, 3, and 4 versus 5, 6, 7, and 8
options.C: 1, 3, 7, and 8 versus 2, 4, 6, and 8
options.D: 1, 3, 5, and 7 versus 2, 4, 6, and 8

why: To test FOOD, compare treatments that differ only in food. The odd-numbered treatments (1, 3, 5, 7) all have oak flowers and the even ones (2, 4, 6, 8) all have oak leaves, with temperature and day length balanced across both groups.

stem: The following question is based on information from Kondo Y. and Kashiwagi A., Experimentally induced autotetraploidy and allotetraploidy in two Japanese pond frogs, Journal of Herpetology 38(3):381 92 (2004). Two researchers experimentally formed tetraploid frogs by fertilizing diploid eggs from Rana porosa brevipoda with diploid sperm from Rana nigromaculata. When they allowed the tetraploid frogs to mate with each other, most of the offspring that survived to maturity were tetraploid, with chromosome sets of both diploid parent species. Based on these results, if this type of tetraploid formed in the wild, what would be the most likely result?

options.A: The tetraploids would be reproductively isolated from both parent species.
options.B: The two parent species would interbreed and fuse into one species.
options.C: The two parent species would recognize each other as mates.
options.D: The tetraploids would invade the habitats of both parental species and cause them to go extinct.

why: The tetraploids mated with each other and produced tetraploid offspring. If they crossed with either diploid parent species, the offspring would be triploid and sterile. So the tetraploids would be reproductively isolated from both parents, which is speciation by allopolyploidy.

stem: New species can sometimes arise via hybridization and subsequent polyploidy. Which of the following describes the likely geographic and reproductive relationships between the hybridizing species?

options.A: The two species are sympatric, but breed during different times of the year.
options.B: The two species are allopatric and breed at different times of the year.
options.C: The two species can be either allopatric or sympatric, but breed during the same seasons of the year.
options.D: The two species are sympatric and breed during the same seasons of the year.

why: To form a hybrid, the two species have to MEET (be sympatric) and be ready to breed at the SAME time. Any choice with different breeding times or allopatry blocks hybridization.

stem: According to the concept of punctuated equilibrium, the "sudden" appearance of a new species in the fossil record means that ________.

options.A: the species will consequently have a relatively short existence compared with other species
options.B: speciation occurred rapidly in geologic time
options.C: the species is now extinct
options.D: speciation occurred in one generation

why: Punctuated equilibrium means long periods of little change broken up by relatively quick speciation. 'Quick' means over tens of thousands of years, fast in GEOLOGIC terms, not in one generation.

stem: Which of the following factors is the primary criterion for determining species boundaries when applying the biological species concept?

options.A: geographic isolation
options.B: gene flow
options.C: morphological similarity
options.D: niche differences

why: The biological species concept defines a species by whether its members can interbreed and exchange genes. So GENE FLOW (or the lack of it) is the boundary.

stem: Dog breeders maintain the purity of breeds by keeping dogs of different breeds apart when they are fertile. This kind of isolation is most similar to which of the following reproductive isolating mechanisms?

options.A: temporal isolation
options.B: habitat isolation
options.C: gametic isolation
options.D: behavioral isolation

why: The breeds can still interbreed; breeders just keep them physically apart so they never meet. Being separated by where they are kept is most like habitat isolation in the answer key.

stem: Almost all peppered moths in England were light colored before the Industrial Revolution. However, some dark forms were collected–the dark color is determined by a single, dominant allele of one gene. The bark of trees became darker during the Industrial Revolution in areas where heavy coal use in factories caused pollution. By about 1900, approximately 90% of the moths around industrial areas were dark, whereas light-colored moths were still abundant elsewhere. Apparently, birds could readily find the light moths against the dark trees in industrial areas and, therefore, were eating more light moths. Recently, use of cleaner fuels has resulted in tree bark becoming lighter again and the dark-colored moths have been disappearing. Which of the following statements best explains whether we should consider the forms different species?

options.A: They are different species–as shown by the fact that natural selection has affected the frequency of the two forms.
options.B: They are NOT different species–as shown by the fact that they live in the same habitats.
options.C: They are different species–as shown by the fact that the two forms are reproductively isolated by habitat.
options.D: They are NOT different species–as shown by the fact that they can interbreed.

why: Light and dark peppered moths still interbreed. They're two forms (morphs) of ONE species, and their frequencies shift with selection. A change in frequency isn't speciation.

stem: Which of the following characteristics is a postzygotic barrier that prevents hybrids between two species from producing offspring?

options.A: hybrid breakdown
options.B: increased hybrid vulnerability
options.C: hybrid gamete isolation
options.D: increased hybrid fertility

why: Hybrid breakdown: the first-generation hybrids are fine and fertile, but their offspring are weak or sterile. It's postzygotic because it acts after fertilization, and it stops the hybrid line from continuing.

stem: Beetle pollinators of a particular plant are attracted to its flowers' bright orange color. The beetles not only pollinate the flowers, but they mate while inside the flowers. A mutant version of the plant with red flowers becomes more common with the passage of time. A particular variant of the beetle prefers the red flowers to the orange flowers. Over time, these two beetle variants diverge from each other to such an extent that interbreeding is no longer possible. Which of the following possible causes of speciation best describes the beetle example and what factor has driven it?

options.A: sympatric speciation; allopolyploidy
options.B: allopatric speciation; behavioral isolation
options.C: allopatric speciation; ecological isolation
options.D: sympatric speciation; habitat differentiation

why: No geographic barrier separates the beetles: they live in the same place (sympatric). They split because each variant prefers a different flower type to mate in, which is habitat differentiation inside one area.

stem: A female fly, full of fertilized eggs, is swept by high winds to an island far from the mainland. She is the first, and only, fly to arrive on this island. Thousands of years later, her numerous offspring occupy the island, but none of them resembles her. There are, instead, several species and their geographic ranges overlap. Each species eats a different kind of food. None of the species can fly and the balancing organs of males differ among species and are now used in courtship displays. Fly species W produces fertile offspring with species Y, but not with species X or Z. Furthermore, X and Z do not hybridize. Which of the following statements about species W and Y is most likely to be accurate?

options.A: Species W and X have more genetic similarity with each other than either does with the other two species.
options.B: Species W and Y will both be selected to avoid mating with each other.
options.C: Species W and Y may fuse into a single species if their hybrids remain fertile over the course of many generations.
options.D: Species W and Y have genomes that are too dissimilar for successful meiosis to occur in hybrid flies.

why: W and Y still produce FERTILE hybrids. If that keeps happening over many generations, gene flow could merge them back into one species, which is called fusion. Reproductive isolation between them isn't complete.

stem: House finches (birds) occurred only in western North America until 1939, when a few individuals were released in New York City. These individuals established a breeding population and gradually expanded their range. The western population also expanded its range somewhat eastward, and the two populations have recently come in contact. Which of the following terms best describes the process that had occurred if the two forms did not interbreed when their expanding ranges met?

options.A: allopatric speciation
options.B: prezygotic isolation
options.C: reinforcement
options.D: sympatric speciation

why: The populations were separated geographically (west vs. New York). When they met again they didn't interbreed, so isolation had already evolved while they were apart. That's allopatric speciation.

stem: Which of the following organisms would be LEAST able to cross a geographic barrier of water that could lead to allopatric speciation?

options.A: birds
options.B: plants with wind-dispersed pollen
options.C: mountain lions
options.D: small rodents

why: Small rodents can't fly, swim well, or ride the wind, so water is a strong barrier for them. Birds, wind-blown pollen and large roaming mammals can cross it more easily.

stem: A team of scientists is trying to understand the evolutionary history of three species of grasses. They hypothesize that Species T is a descendent of a hybrid between Species R and Species S. Which of the following experimental approaches would best help elucidate the evolutionary history of these three species?

options.A: Hybridize Species R and S; induce tetraploidy in the hybrids; and compare the hybrids to Species T.
options.B: Hybridize Species R and S; plant the hybrid offspring in environmental conditions similar to those of Species R; follow the morphological and genetic changes in the offspring of the hybrids; and compare any observed changes to Species R.
options.C: Sequence the DNA of all three species and determine which alleles are unique to each species.
options.D: Hybridize Species R and S; plant the hybrid offspring in environmental conditions resembling those of Species R, S, and T; follow morphological and genetic changes in the offspring of the hybrids; and compare the observed changes to Species T.

why: To test whether T came from a hybrid of R and S, recreate the hybrid and let it evolve in conditions like R's, S's and T's habitats, then track whether it becomes T-like. Choice D covers all three environments. Choice C only lists differences and doesn't test the history.

stem: Lions and tigers sometimes breed in zoos, but hybrids have not been seen in nature and even in zoos they do not reproduce well. Which of the following statements is the best conclusion that can be derived from this information?

options.A: The morphological or ecological species concepts must be used rather than the biological species concept because there could be gene flow between the species in nature.
options.B: The biological species concept can be applied because species are, in part, defined by the inability to produce viable, fertile offspring with other species.
options.C: The biological species concept is invalid because hybrids can be formed.
options.D: Lions and tigers are not actually different species because they can produce viable offspring in captivity.

why: The biological species concept is about what happens in NATURE. Lions and tigers don't hybridize in the wild, and zoo hybrids reproduce poorly, so they still count as separate species.

stem: Two species of frogs belonging to the same genus occasionally mate, but the embryos stop developing after a day and then die. Which of the following mechanisms keep the species separate?

options.A: gametic isolation
options.B: reduced hybrid viability
options.C: reduced hybrid fertility
options.D: hybrid breakdown

why: The embryos form but die after a day. Fertilization happened, but the hybrid doesn't survive, which is reduced hybrid VIABILITY. Reduced fertility would mean hybrids live but can't reproduce.

stem: Which of the following outcomes is most likely in hybrid zones where reinforcement of isolating mechanisms is occurring?

options.A: increased gene flow between distinct gene pools
options.B: a decrease in the genetic distinctness of two gene pools
options.C: speciation
options.D: formation of a stable hybrid zone

why: Reinforcement: hybrids are less fit, so selection strengthens prezygotic barriers. The two gene pools become MORE distinct, which completes speciation.

stem: Males of different species of the fruit fly Drosophila that live in the same parts of the Hawaiian Islands have different elaborate courtship rituals. These rituals involve fighting other males and making stylized movements that attract females. What type of reproductive isolation does this represent?

options.A: gametic isolation
options.B: habitat isolation
options.C: behavioral isolation
options.D: temporal isolation

why: Different courtship rituals mean females don't recognize males of other species as mates. Isolation through mating behavior is behavioral isolation.

stem: Plant species A has a diploid chromosome number of 12. Plant species B has a diploid number of 16. A new species, C, arises as an allopolyploid from A and B. The diploid number for species C would probably be ________.
why: An allopolyploid keeps BOTH parents' full diploid sets: 12 + 16 = 28. A normal hybrid would get half from each, 6 + 8 = 14 (choice C), and would be sterile.

stem: Which of the following factors would not contribute to allopatric speciation?

options.A: The separated population is small, and genetic drift occurs.
options.B: Gene flow between the two populations is extensive.
options.C: The isolated population is exposed to different selection pressures than the ancestral population.
options.D: Different mutations begin to distinguish the gene pools of the separated populations.

why: Allopatric speciation needs gene flow to be CUT OFF. Extensive gene flow keeps the populations mixed and works against speciation. Drift, different selection and new mutations all push them apart.

stem: Bird guides once listed the myrtle warbler and Audubon's warbler as distinct species. Recently, these birds have been classified as eastern and western forms of a single species, the yellow-rumped warbler. Which of the following pieces of evidence, if true, would be cause for this reclassification?

options.A: The two forms have many genes in common.
options.B: The two forms live in similar habitats and have similar food requirements.
options.C: The two forms interbreed often in nature, and their offspring survive and reproduce well.
options.D: The two forms are very similar in appearance.

why: They interbreed freely in nature and their offspring are fertile, so they meet the biological species concept's definition of one species. Similar genes, looks or habitats don't decide it.

stem: The largest unit within which gene flow can readily occur is a ________.

options.A: species
options.B: hybrid
options.C: genus
options.D: population

why: A species is the largest group whose members can share genes by interbreeding. A population is a smaller, local group within a species.

stem: Which factor most likely caused animals and plants in India to differ greatly from species in nearby southeast Asia?

options.A: India was a separate continent until 45 million years ago.
options.B: The climates of the two regions are similar.
options.C: Life in India was wiped out by ancient volcanic eruptions.
options.D: India is in the process of separating from the rest of Asia.

why: India was an island continent drifting north for a long time before it hit Asia (about 45 million years ago). Its species evolved in isolation, so they differ from nearby Southeast Asian species. That's plate tectonics affecting biogeography.

stem: Natural selection, operating on which of the following genetic changes, most likely resulted in the loss of ventral spines in modern freshwater sticklebacks?

options.A: silencing of the Pitx1 gene
options.B: point mutations in the Pitx1 gene
options.C: deletion of the Pitx1 gene
options.D: duplication of the Pitx1 gene

why: Freshwater sticklebacks still have a working Pitx1 gene, but it's switched OFF in the tissue that builds pelvic spines. The change is in gene REGULATION (silencing), not a deleted or mutated gene.

stem: Which of the following statements best describes the evolution of complex eyes?

options.A: Complex eyes arose fully formed.
options.B: Complex eyes evolved through a series of steps that improved the functioning of the eyes.
options.C: Eyes in mollucs and vertebrates are descended from the same common ancestor.
options.D: The evolution of mollusc eyes was dependent on the evolution of vertebrate eyes.

why: Complex eyes built up through many small steps, from light-sensitive patches to cups to lenses, and each step was useful. Mollusk and vertebrate eyes evolved independently.

stem: Which of the following characteristics were most likely present in the first animals that colonized land?

options.A: ability to resist dehydration and eat producers
options.B: ability to resist dehydration and presence of a spine
options.C: ability to eat producers and support themselves on four limbs
options.D: ability to resist dehydration and support themselves on four limbs

why: Out of water, the first threats are drying out and needing food. Early land animals (like arthropods) had to resist dehydration and eat land producers. Spines and four limbs came later, in vertebrates.

stem: Which of the following molecules was most likely the first genetic material on Earth?

options.A: oligopeptides located within protocells
options.B: self-replicating RNA molecules with catalytic activity
options.C: DNA produced by reverse transcriptase from abiotically produced RNA
options.D: DNA molecules whose information was transcribed to RNA and later translated in polypeptides

why: In the 'RNA world' hypothesis, RNA came first because it can both store information AND act as an enzyme (ribozymes). DNA and proteins came later.

stem: Many species of snakes lay eggs. However, in the forests of northern Minnesota, where the growing season is short, only live-bearing snake species are present. Which of the following processes most likely resulted in the differences in snake reproduction?

options.A: natural selection leading to exaptations
options.B: species selection
options.C: goal direction in evolution
options.D: sexual selection

why: Species that give birth to live young survive better where the season is short, while egg-laying species fail there. Whole species differ in survival depending on a trait, which is species selection.

stem: If one organ is an exaptation of another organ, then which of the following statements is most accurate?

options.A: The two organs are homologous.
options.B: The two organs occur in the same species.
options.C: The two organs have the same function.
options.D: The two organs are undergoing convergent evolution.

why: An exaptation is a structure that evolved for one use and was later co-opted for another, like feathers (warmth, then flight). It's the same inherited structure, so the two versions are homologous.

stem: Which of the following did all protocells have in common?

options.A: the ability to synthesize enzymes
options.B: RNA genes
options.C: a surrounding membrane or membrane-like structure
options.D: the ability to replicate RNA

why: By definition a protocell is a collection of molecules inside a membrane-like boundary (such as a lipid vesicle). Enzymes, RNA genes and replication weren't necessarily present in all of them.

stem: Which of the following statements provides the best evidence that the fossil record is an incomplete record of evolution?

options.A: The fossil record is biased for organisms that had hard shells and skeletons.
options.B: The fossil record shows changes in kinds of organisms that lived on earth.
options.C: Fossils document how new organisms come from preexisting organisms.
options.D: The fossil record shows that many animals are extinct.

why: Soft-bodied organisms rarely fossilize, so the record over-represents hard shells and bones. That bias is why the fossil record is incomplete. The other choices are things the record DOES show.

stem: The prokaryotic flagellum is a complex structure consisting of several dozen different proteins. Which of the following statements best describes the origin of flagella in prokaryotes?

options.A: The need for more complex structure must have driven evolution.
options.B: Ancestral versions of this protein assemblage were either less functional or had different functions than modern prokaryotic flagella.
options.C: Natural selection cannot account for the evolution of the prokaryotic flagellum.
options.D: Flagella could not have arisen by evolution because the structure is too complex to have evolved gradually.

why: Complex structures evolve from simpler ancestral versions that worked differently or had other jobs; some flagellar proteins resemble secretion-system proteins. Evolution doesn't respond to 'need' (choice A).

stem: Four sediment cores were removed from the floor of an inland sea. The sea was in existence intermittently throughout the entire time that terrestrial life has existed. Researchers wish to locate and study the terrestrial organisms fossilized in these cores. In the diagram, the cores are illustrated as vertical columns, with the top of the column representing the most recent strata and the bottom representing the time when land was first colonized by life. Which of the following factors would best allow a researcher to assign absolute dates to the fossils in the sediments?

options.A: knowledge that the sediments had not been affected by underwater currents during their deposition
options.B: equal spacing of fossils throughout the columns
options.C: presence of volcanic ash layers between the sedimentary strata
options.D: knowledge of the order in which the fossils were deposited

why: Absolute dates need radiometric dating. Volcanic ash layers can be dated (with potassium-argon, for example), and fossils between two dated ash layers can be bracketed. Order of layers only gives RELATIVE ages.

stem: Which of the following statements is accurate with regard to the Cambrian explosion?

options.A: The Cambrian explosion is evidence for the instantaneous creation of life on Earth.
options.B: There are fossils of animals in geological strata that are older than the Cambrian explosion.
options.C: Only the fossils of microorganisms occur in geological strata older than the Cambrian explosion.
options.D: The Cambrian explosion marks the appearance of filter-feeding animals in the fossil record.

why: Animal fossils (the Ediacaran biota) exist in rocks OLDER than the Cambrian. The explosion was a rapid diversification, not the first appearance of animals.

stem: Which of the following methods is the most accurate way to measure the age of a relatively recent fossil?

options.A: ratio of carbon-14 to carbon-12
options.B: sequences of fossils in rock strata
options.C: ratio of uranium-238 to thorium-234
options.D: ratio of plutonium-244 to uranium 240

why: For relatively young organic remains (up to about 50,000–75,000 years old), carbon-14 dating is the most accurate. Uranium methods suit much older rocks.

stem: Which of the following outcomes is the most likely evolutionary effect of duplication of homeotic Hox genes?

options.A: It allowed the reversal of the head-tail orientation of animals.
options.B: It permitted the evolution of novel forms.
options.C: It reduced morphological diversity of simple forms of life.
options.D: It caused the extinction of major groups.

why: Hox genes control body layout. Extra copies could take on new roles, allowing new body plans, which means more diversity.

stem: Mycorrhizae are symbiotic associations between some fungi and the roots of many plants. Which of the following experiments best would test whether a plant benefits from the presence of the fungus?

options.A: Grow many individuals of Plant X in shaded and unshaded conditions. Then compare the average plant size and average number of seeds produced between the two groups.
options.B: Grow many individuals of Plant X with and without its fungus. Then compare the average plant size and average number of seeds produced between the two groups.
options.C: Grow many individuals of Plant X with two different species of fungi. Then compare the average plant size and average number of seeds produced between the two groups.
options.D: Grow many individuals of Plant X and Plant Y without any fungus. Then compare the average plant size and average number of seeds produced between the two groups.

why: A good experiment changes ONE variable. Grow the same plant with and without the fungus and compare growth and seeds. The other designs change the wrong variable or include no fungus at all.

stem: The temporal fenestra in the skulls in fossils of ancestral mammals changed in shape and size over time. These changes were most likely due to changes in the muscles that closed the jaws. Which of the following research approaches would be most helpful for understanding the evolutionary benefits of these changes?

options.A: comparing changes in the fenestra with changes in the jaw hinge
options.B: correlating the fenestra size with changes in the shape of the teeth
options.C: comparing the changes in the fenestra in the fossils leading to mammals with the changes in the fossils leading to modern reptiles
options.D: correlating the strength of jaw closure and the size and hardness of potential prey

why: The question is about the BENEFIT of changes in jaw muscles. Relating bite strength to the kind of prey available shows what advantage stronger jaws gave.

stem: Hawaii is the youngest and most southeastern of the seven largest Hawaiian islands the oldest islands lie to the northwest. Kauai is the oldest and most northwestern big island. Hawaii is also closest to, and Kauai furthest from, the seafloor spreading center from which the Pacific plate originates, which lies about 5,600 km southeast of the island of Hawaii. Assuming equal rates of sedimentation from the islands onto the sea floor, which of the following places is the most likely location of the thickest sediment layer and thus the area with the greatest diversity of fossils above the oceanic crust?

options.A: between the island of Hawaii and the seafloor spreading center
options.B: around the base of Kauai
options.C: around the base of the island of Hawaii
options.D: in the area where the islands are most concentrated (highest number of islands per unit surface area)

why: Kauai is the oldest island, so sediment has been piling up around its base the longest. Equal rates over more time give the thickest layer and the most fossils.

stem: Which period had the greatest increase in the number of extant marine animal families?

options.A: Permian
options.B: Paleozoic
options.C: Cenozoic
options.D: Mesozoic

why: Marine family diversity rose most steeply during the Mesozoic and on into the Cenozoic. The key says Mesozoic. (Strictly, the Mesozoic is an era, not a period.)

stem: Which of the following statements accurately describes the effect of the Permian and Cretaceous extinctions on the percentage of prey organisms in marine environments?

options.A: After the Permian extinction the percentage of prey organisms remained stable, but after the Cretaceous extinction the percentage of prey organisms increased.
options.B: After the Permian extinction the percentage of prey organisms decreased, but after the Cretaceous extinction the percentage of prey organisms continuously increased.
options.C: After the Permian and Cretaceous extinctions, the percentages of prey organisms increased.
options.D: After both the Permian and Cretaceous extinctions, the percentages of prey organisms decreased.

why: Mass extinctions knock down every group, prey included. The figure shows the percentage of prey organisms dropping after both the Permian and Cretaceous extinctions. (Open the PDF to see the graph.)

stem: Which of the following statements best explains the existence of evolutionary trends, such as increasing body sizes among horse species?

options.A: A larger volume-to-surface area ratio is adaptive in many mammals.
options.B: In particular environments, similar adaptations can be beneficial to more than one species.
options.C: Evolution generally progresses toward some goal.
options.D: Evolution tends toward increased complexity or increased size.

why: Trends like bigger horse bodies happen when similar conditions favor similar adaptations in several related species. Evolution has no built-in goal and no drive toward bigger or more complex (choices C and D).
